X_11
====

.. rubric:: FEUERBACH POINT

.. container:: etc-identity-bar

   ``feuerbach_point(A, B, C) -> X_11`` • **Feuerbach (1822)** • **Kimberling** ``X(11)`` • **Search** :math:`(6,9,13)`: :math:`\frac{256 \sqrt{35}}{573} \approx 2.643135121245`

.. enunciation::

   :ref:`X_11 <X_11>` is the point of tangency of the nine-point circle and the incircle. The nine-point circle is the circumcenter of the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`, as well as the :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>`. Feuerbach's famous theorem states that the nine-point circle is tangent to the incircle and the three excircles.

.. figure:: x-00011.svg
   :alt: X_11 — FEUERBACH POINT
   :align: center

   **X_11** (*FEUERBACH POINT*) constructed at :g:`X_11 <X_11>` = :math:`\left(6,\; 8\right)` in exact rational coordinates on Heronian :math:`(15, 13, 14)` over :math:`\mathbb{Q}` with vertices :g:`A <A>` = :math:`(0, 0)`, :g:`B <B>` = :math:`(14, 0)`, :g:`C <C>` = :math:`(5, 12)`, area :math:`\Delta = 84`. Switch view modes or reference triangles above.

.. container:: etc-mode-four-triangles

   Across the canonical algebraic number fields — :g:`Heronian (15, 13, 14) <heronian-X_11>` over :math:`\mathbb{Q}` (:math:`X_{11} = \left(6,\; 8\right)`), :g:`Right (3, 4, 5) <right-X_11>` over :math:`\mathbb{Q}` (:math:`X_{11} = \left(1,\; 2\right)`), :g:`Kepler (1, √φ, φ) <kepler-X_11>` over :math:`\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{\phi})`, :g:`Kimberling (6, 9, 13) <kimberling-X_11>` over :math:`\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{35})` (:math:`X_{11} = \left(\frac{21184}{2483},\; \frac{36 \sqrt{35}}{2483}\right)`), :g:`Golden (φ, φ, 1) <golden-X_11>` over :math:`\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5 + 2\sqrt{5}})` (:math:`X_{11} = \left(\frac{1}{2},\; 0\right)`), and :g:`Gnomon (1, 1, φ) <gnomon-X_11>` over :math:`\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5 + 2\sqrt{5}})` (:math:`X_{11} = \left(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{\sqrt{5}}{4},\; 0\right)`) — **X_11** lies strictly interior on Heronian, Right, Kepler, Kimberling while crossing outside :math:`\triangle ABC` on Golden, Gnomon (where signed sub-areas change sign across the sidelines while still summing algebraically to :math:`\Delta`). On the **Equilateral (2, 2, 2)** limit over :math:`\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{3})`, **X_11** becomes indeterminate (:math:`0 : 0 : 0`) under :math:`D_3` symmetry.
